policy: While any blocker below is open, this repository must not publish a Form Package, an Interface or Binding Definition, a provider release that exposes the family resource types, or a lifecycle transition for any family Form. Closing a blocker requires the evidence it names, not a passing local gate. The freeze is scoped to this lane's artifacts: it never gates the retained v1alpha1/v1alpha2 packages, and it never gates the append-only security revocation path, because an urgent revocation for an already-published package must not wait on this lane's readiness.

blockers.title: A real host preserves the exact FormRef
blockers.rationale: The provider dispatches read, update and delete on the ref recorded in state. Until a host outside this repository answers for an exact ref rather than for a kind, that dispatch is unproven against anything but the reference host.

blockers.title: A relation pins the target's contract, not only its incarnation
blockers.rationale: A reference pins the resolved target UID, so a re-created target is not adopted silently. It does not yet pin what contract that target satisfies, so a target whose Definition moves incompatibly still satisfies the reference.

blockers.title: Runtime loadable media types and artifact manifest media types agree
blockers.rationale: The runtime ABI and the artifact manifest each state a media-type set, and they disagree. A bundle can therefore be accepted by one and unusable by the other.

blockers.title: An independent host implements Host API v1alpha3
blockers.rationale: The only implementation of this lane is the disposable reference host inside this repository. A lane with one implementation, written by the same people who wrote the contract, has not shown that its contract is implementable by anyone else.

blockers.title: A real backend materialises bundle, version and deployment
blockers.rationale: Immutable revisions and weighted traffic are these Forms' whole value. Until a real backend performs them, the state machine is asserted rather than demonstrated.

blockers.title: A real backend materialises an edge KV namespace and its typed binding
blockers.rationale: A binding projects an API into a running isolate. Nothing in this repository can prove that projection; only a real runtime can.

blockers.title: A worker is reachable over HTTPS without a customer-owned domain
blockers.rationale: Requiring a verified custom domain before the first request makes the shortest path to a working worker longer than the path to abandoning it.

blockers.title: A real runtime is measured against the ABI contract
blockers.rationale: The Host API lane proves that a host states which ABI it implements and holds desired state to it. It does not prove that an isolate behaves that way. conformance/runtime-abi-v1 is the corpus that measures one, and its existence is not this blocker closing: what closes it is a passed deployed-runtime-conformance-run, with the module-loader lane measured, against a runtime this repository does not own. A run against the repository's in-process stand-in proves the corpus and never a runtime, and every report says which of the two it is (decision 0023).

blockers.title: A provider lifecycle runs end to end against an independent host
blockers.rationale: Create, roll out, promote, roll back, observe, recover from an interrupted apply, and destroy must be demonstrated as one sequence against a host this repository does not own, because the failure modes worth catching only appear between the steps.

blockers.title: Destroy completes through a real backend and leaves nothing orphaned
blockers.rationale: A platform that cannot reliably delete what it created is not one anybody should adopt. An orphan scan finding nothing, against a real backend, is the evidence.

blockers.title: The ABI declares a tail handler nothing can activate
blockers.rationale: worker.runtime@1.0.0 declares a tail handler, and no resource in this family activates one: the three inward-activation attachments are WorkerCustomDomain (fetch), WorkerCronTrigger (scheduled) and QueueConsumer (queue). No deployment a portable author can write causes a host to invoke tail, so no conformance run can observe it and two hosts could implement it differently with nothing able to detect the divergence — the same defect as the runtime-selector field decision 0019 removed from WorkerVersion. The runtime corpus records it as explicitly unmeasured rather than silently unchecked. It closes by removing tail from the ABI's declaredHandlers vocabulary in a new exact Interface version, or by adding the Form that attaches a tail consumer; the removal changes Interface bytes and regenerates the Form chain, so it belongs to that regeneration (decision 0023).
